<!--
Step 04 of the workflow. Computes two indicators from the PAIRED scenario ensembles
produced by 03_Scenarios_Through_time.Rmd (saved as sims_factual / sims_counter):
  (1) per-species MEAN INDIVIDUAL WEIGHT through time (size-structure indicator),
      factual (seal increase) vs counterfactual (seals held at 1978);
  (2) MODEL SKILL = Spearman correlation of modelled vs observed biomass across the
      ensemble, factual vs counterfactual.
Current dimensions: 1978-2024 (47 yr), all 19 species, per-species survey cutoffs.
(Journal style: no plot titles/subtitles; notes/interpretation as comments.)
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)
library(mizer)
library(mizerExperimental)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())   # portable project root
save_dir <- paste0(here::here(), "/Ess_Output/")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Inputs — factual model + paired scenario ensembles (from step 03)

```{r inputs}
# Factual Stage-2 model (for species set + per-species survey cutoffs)
params <- readRDS(if (file.exists("Ess_data/params_stage2_AUTO.RDS"))
                    "Ess_data/params_stage2_AUTO.RDS" else
                    "Ess_data/params_stage2_factual.RDS")

# Paired ensembles from 03 (same randomised web under both scenarios):
#   sims_factual = seal effort increases 1978->2024
#   sims_counter = seal effort held constant at the 1978 level (the counterfactual)
sims_factual <- readRDS("Ess_Output/sims_factual.RDS")
sims_counter <- readRDS("Ess_Output/sims_counter.RDS")

# Observed survey biomass (g) for the skill comparison
biomass_ts <- readRDS("Ess_data/biomass_ts.RDS")

sp    <- species_params(params)$species
cl    <- species_params(params)$biomass_cutoff;     cl[is.na(cl)] <- 0    # lower survey cutoff
ch    <- species_params(params)$biomass_cutoffHigh; ch[is.na(ch)] <- Inf  # upper survey cutoff
wm    <- species_params(params)$w_mat                                     # maturation weight (g)
w     <- params@w; dw <- params@dw
n_sims <- length(sims_factual)
cat(sprintf("Ensemble size: %d factual, %d counterfactual paired members\n",
            length(sims_factual), length(sims_counter)))
```

## Consistently-sampled size window per species (fixed, for a robust mean-weight comparison)

```{r obs-size-window}
# Survey COMMON_NAME -> mizer species; per-species allometry, cutoffs, maturation weight.
species_code_lookup <- c(
  "COD(ATLANTIC)"="Atlantic Cod","HADDOCK"="Haddock","WHITE HAKE"="White Hake",
  "SILVER HAKE"="Silver Hake","POLLOCK"="Pollock","REDFISH UNSEPARATED"="Redfish Unseparated",
  "AMERICAN PLAICE"="American Plaice","YELLOWTAIL FLOUNDER"="Yellowtail Flounder",
  "SPINY DOGFISH"="Spiny Dogfish","HALIBUT(ATLANTIC)"="Atlantic Halibut",
  "SQUIRREL OR RED HAKE"="Red Hake","MONKFISH,GOOSEFISH,ANGLER"="Monkfish",
  "NORTHERN SAND LANCE"="Sand Lance","WITCH FLOUNDER"="Witch Flounder",
  "HERRING(ATLANTIC)"="Atlantic Herring","THORNY SKATE"="Thorny Skate",
  "WINTER SKATE"="Winter Skate","LONGHORN SCULPIN"="Longhorn Sculpin","CAPELIN"="Capelin")

ab_obs <- tibble(Species = sp, a = species_params(params)$a, b = species_params(params)$b,
                 cl = cl, ch = ch, wmat = wm)

# ============================================================================================
# CONSISTENTLY-SAMPLED SIZE WINDOW  (the ">= 75%" rule)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT the 75% is:
#   A size class = a 2-cm length bin. A bin is "consistently sampled" for a species if the
#   survey caught that species in that bin in AT LEAST 75% of survey years (>= 36 of 47 yr).
#   Each species' analysis window is the full span [min, max] of its consistently-sampled bins.
#
# WHAT it is used for:
#   It defines the size range over which the size-structure indicator (mean individual weight,
#   below) is computed and compared between the MODEL and the SURVEY. Both the modelled and the
#   observed mean weight are restricted to this identical, species-specific window.
#
# WHY 75% (and why a fixed window, not a moving one):
#   The bottom-trawl survey does NOT sample all sizes equally every year: it under-catches the
#   smallest fish (gear selectivity) and, especially for collapsed stocks, the largest fish
#   (availability), and which extreme sizes appear varies year to year. Restricting to bins
#   present in >= 75% of years therefore (a) keeps only the sizes the survey samples reliably,
#   (b) trims BOTH sporadically-caught extremes (recruit pulses at the small end, rare large
#   fish at the large end) so neither dominates the mean, and (c) uses ONE FIXED window per
#   species (not re-derived each year), so it adds no year-to-year window noise and is NOT
#   circular — it is never re-fit per year to force the model onto the data.
#   75% is a single uniform threshold for all species; internal gaps are tolerated (model and
#   observed use the same span). The 3 sparsely-sampled species with no bin reaching 75%
#   (Atlantic Halibut, Capelin, Winter Skate) fall back to the fixed gear cutoffs cl/ch.
#
# SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the window is computed once by Ess_data/make_size_windows.R and
# saved to Ess_data/size_windows.csv, which BOTH 03 (species/community size spectra) and 04
# (mean weight, here) load — so every size-based model/observed comparison uses the SAME window.
# ============================================================================================
win_tbl <- read.csv("Ess_data/size_windows.csv")            # Species, thr_used, Lmin, Lmax, wlo, whi
wlo <- setNames(win_tbl$wlo, win_tbl$Species)[sp]
whi <- setNames(win_tbl$whi, win_tbl$Species)[sp]
print(win_tbl %>% transmute(Species, thr_used, Lmin, Lmax, wlo = round(wlo), whi = round(whi)))
```

# Read abundance by species
```{r}
# read abundance by species (survey numbers per species-year)
abundance_obs <- read.csv("Ess_data/abundance_obs.csv")
# Make sure Species types match for the join
abundance_long <- abundance_obs %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = levels(biomass_ts$Species)))

# Join and compute mean weight
mean_weight_ts <- biomass_ts %>%
  left_join(abundance_long, by = c("Year", "Species")) %>%
  mutate(MeanWeight = Biomass / Abundance)
```


## Per-sim mean individual weight over each species' consistently-sampled size window

```{r indicator-helper}
# For one MizerSim: per species & year, mean individual weight (g) = biomass / numbers,
# computed over that species' FIXED consistently-sampled window [wlo, whi] (the >=90%-of-years
# size classes from above). The fixed window trims both the recruit-pulse small end and the
# rare-giant large end, so neither extreme dominates the mean.
sim_indicators <- function(sim) {
  st <- as.integer(dimnames(sim@n)[[1]])
  wB <- w * dw
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sp), function(j) {
    idx <- w >= wlo[j] & w <= whi[j]                                    # fixed survey window
    B <- rowSums(sweep(sim@n[, j, idx, drop = FALSE], 3, wB[idx], "*")) # g
    N <- rowSums(sweep(sim@n[, j, idx, drop = FALSE], 3, dw[idx], "*")) # numbers
    data.frame(Species = sp[j], Year = st, Biomass = B, Number = N,
               MeanWeight = B / N)
  }))
}

# Apply across an ensemble, tagging the sim index and scenario.
ensemble_indicators <- function(sims, scenario) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sims), function(k) {
    d <- sim_indicators(sims[[k]]); d$sim <- k; d$scen <- scenario; d
  }))
}

df_all <- bind_rows(
  ensemble_indicators(sims_factual, "Factual (seal increase)"),
  ensemble_indicators(sims_counter, "Counterfactual (seals constant)"))

```

```{r}
# ── OBSERVED mean individual weight over each species' FIXED consistently-sampled window
#    [wlo, whi] (the >=90%-of-years size classes). Built from the length-frequency survey
#    data (LF_Biomass_Abund.csv). species_code_lookup / ab_obs / win_tbl are defined above.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mean_weight_ts <- read.csv("Ess_data/LF_Biomass_Abund.csv") %>%
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466,
         YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 2024) %>%
  mutate(Species   = species_code_lookup[COMMON_NAME],
         length_cm = ifelse(COMMON_NAME == "HERRING(ATLANTIC)", FLEN / 10, FLEN)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Species)) %>%
  left_join(ab_obs, by = "Species") %>%
  left_join(win_tbl %>% select(Species, wlo, whi), by = "Species") %>%   # fixed window
  mutate(w = a * length_cm^b, Bg = Biomass_Strata_KG * 1e3,
         flo = ifelse(is.na(wlo), cl, wlo),
         fhi = ifelse(is.na(whi), ch, whi)) %>%
  filter(w >= flo, w <= fhi) %>%   # SAME fixed window as the model
  group_by(Year = YEAR, Species) %>%
  summarise(Btot = sum(Bg,              na.rm = TRUE),
            Ntot = sum(Abundance_Strata, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(MeanWeight = Btot / Ntot) %>%
  filter(is.finite(MeanWeight), MeanWeight > 0) %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = levels(biomass_ts$Species)))
```

## Indicator 1 — mean individual weight over consistently-sampled sizes, factual vs counterfactual

```{r mean-weight}
# Ensemble median + 10-90% band (the band is the ensemble spread across randomised
# food webs, NOT a formal CI). Factual vs counterfactual overlaid per species.
# ── SUMMARISE ENSEMBLE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mw <- df_all %>%
  filter(is.finite(MeanWeight), MeanWeight > 0) %>%
  group_by(scen, Species, Year) %>%
  summarise(med = median(MeanWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo  = quantile(MeanWeight, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi  = quantile(MeanWeight, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = levels(mean_weight_ts$Species))) %>%
  arrange(Species, Year)

# ── PLOT (manuscript Fig 5 style) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reference period (<= 1986) drawn in grey — the counterfactual (seals held at 1978)
# is the "no seal change" reference condition; scenarios are shown coloured only for
# the projection (>= 1986), with a dashed divider between the two.
divider <- 1986
mw_ref  <- mw %>% filter(scen == "Counterfactual (seals constant)", Year <= divider)
mw_proj <- mw %>% filter(Year >= divider)

p_mw <- ggplot() +
  # dashed reference / projection divider
  geom_vline(xintercept = divider, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # reference period — grey band + line
  geom_ribbon(data = mw_ref, aes(Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi,
              fill = "Reference period (1978–1985)"), alpha = 0.40) +
  geom_line(data = mw_ref, aes(Year, med,
            colour = "Reference period (1978–1985)"), linewidth = 0.6) +
  # projection period — coloured scenarios (10–90% ensemble band + median)
  geom_ribbon(data = mw_proj, aes(Year, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = scen),
              alpha = 0.20, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(data = mw_proj, aes(Year, med, colour = scen), linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Observed mean weight (survey, same fixed window) — black points
  geom_point(data = mean_weight_ts, aes(x = Year, y = MeanWeight),
             colour = "black", size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = c(
    "Reference period (1978–1985)" = "grey40",
    "Factual (seal increase)"           = "firebrick",
    "Counterfactual (seals constant)"   = "steelblue")) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(
    "Reference period (1978–1985)" = "grey70",
    "Factual (seal increase)"           = "firebrick",
    "Counterfactual (seals constant)"   = "steelblue")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean individual weight (g), consistently-sampled sizes") +
  theme(
    text             = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title       = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border     = element_rect(linewidth = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank() )

p_mw
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "indicator_mean_weight.jpeg"),
 p_mw, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 200)

# INTERPRETATION (comment): mean individual weight over each species' consistently-sampled
# size window (2-cm classes present in >=90% of survey years, contiguous core). The window is
# FIXED (not re-derived per year), so it adds no year-to-year window noise and is not circular,
# and it trims both the recruit-pulse small end and rare-giant large end so neither dominates.
# Where the counterfactual (blue) sits above the factual (red), removing the seal increase
# leaves a larger-bodied size structure. Bands = 10-90% of ensemble webs.
```

fixed >=90%-consistently-sampled window (above) is now the single size-structure indicator. -->

## Model skill assessment (biomass, catch, mean weight vs observed)

```{r skill-inputs}
# Observed survey biomass (g) — reloaded here for the skill comparison section
biomass_ts <- readRDS("Ess_data/biomass_ts.RDS")

# Observed survey biomass and catches per species-year, rescaled (g -> Mt, /1e9)
obs <- biomass_ts |> transmute(Species, Year, Biomass_obs = Biomass / 1e9)
obs_catch <- readRDS("Ess_data/yield_ts.RDS") |>
  filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>  # no reliable catch data for these
  transmute(Species, Year, Yield_obs = Yield / 1e9)
```

### Modelled fishing catch

```{r sim-catch-fn}
# Modelled fishing catch per ensemble member (sum over fishing gears, excl. Seals) — g
fish_gears <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic")
sim_catch <- function(sim) {
  yg <- getYieldGear(sim)                                   # [time, gear, species]
  fy <- apply(yg[, dimnames(yg)[[2]] %in% fish_gears, , drop = FALSE], c(1, 3), sum)  # sum over fishing gears only
  st <- as.integer(rownames(fy))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sp),
                        function(j) data.frame(Species = sp[j], Year = st, Yield = fy[, j])))
}

# Apply sim_catch() across every ensemble member, tagging sim index + scenario
ensemble_catch <- function(sims, scenario) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sims), function(k) {
    d <- sim_catch(sims[[k]]); d$sim <- k; d$scen <- scenario; d }))
}

df_catches <- bind_rows(
  ensemble_catch(sims_factual, "Factual (seal increase)"),
  ensemble_catch(sims_counter, "Counterfactual (seals constant)"))

```

### Skill metrics: Spearman rho and log-scale RMSE

```{r skill-metrics}
# Simple RMSE helper, used on log-transformed values below
rmse <- function(pred, obs) sqrt(mean((pred - obs)^2, na.rm = TRUE))

# Per ensemble member: Spearman rho and log-scale RMSE for biomass (modelled vs observed)
skill_biomass <- df_all |>
  mutate(Biomass = Biomass / 1e9) |>
  inner_join(obs, by = c("Species", "Year")) |>
  filter(Biomass_obs > 0, Biomass > 0, Year >= 1986, Year <= 2024) |>  # skip zero/negative & pre-1986 years
  group_by(scen, sim) |>
  summarise(rho_biomass  = cor(Biomass, Biomass_obs, method = "spearman"),
            rmse_biomass = rmse(log(Biomass), log(Biomass_obs)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Per ensemble member: Spearman rho and log-scale RMSE for catches (modelled vs observed)
skill_catch <- df_catches |>
  mutate(Yield = Yield / 1e9) |>
  inner_join(obs_catch, by = c("Species", "Year")) |>
  filter(Yield_obs > 0, Yield > 0, Year >= 1986, Year <= 2024) |>
  group_by(scen, sim) |>
  summarise(rho_catch  = cor(Yield, Yield_obs, method = "spearman"),
            rmse_catch = rmse(log(Yield), log(Yield_obs)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Per ensemble member: Spearman rho and log-scale RMSE for mean individual weight,
# against OBSERVED mean weight (mean_weight_ts), consistent in structure
# with biomass and catch above.
skill_mw <- df_all |>
  filter(!is.na(MeanWeight), MeanWeight > 0) |>
  inner_join(
    mean_weight_ts |> transmute(Species, Year, MeanWeight_obs = MeanWeight),
    by = c("Species", "Year")) |>
  filter(MeanWeight_obs > 0, MeanWeight > 0, Year >= 1986, Year <= 2024) |>
  group_by(scen, sim) |>
  summarise(rho_mw  = cor(MeanWeight, MeanWeight_obs, method = "spearman"),
            rmse_mw = rmse(log(MeanWeight), log(MeanWeight_obs)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Combine all skill metrics: Spearman rho and log-scale RMSE across all 3 indicators,
# reshaped long for faceted plotting below
skill <- left_join(skill_biomass, skill_catch, by = c("scen", "sim")) |>
  left_join(skill_mw, by = c("scen", "sim")) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(rho_biomass, rho_catch, rho_mw,
                        rmse_biomass, rmse_catch, rmse_mw),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    indicator = case_when(
      metric %in% c("rho_biomass", "rmse_biomass") ~ "Biomass",
      metric %in% c("rho_catch", "rmse_catch")      ~ "Catch",
      metric %in% c("rho_mw", "rmse_mw")            ~ "Mean individual weight"),
    stat_type = case_when(
      metric %in% c("rho_biomass", "rho_catch", "rho_mw")    ~ "Spearman rho",
      metric %in% c("rmse_biomass", "rmse_catch", "rmse_mw") ~ "RMSE (log-scale)"),
    indicator = factor(indicator, levels = c("Biomass", "Catch", "Mean individual weight")),
    stat_type = factor(stat_type, levels = c("Spearman rho", "RMSE (log-scale)")))
```

### Skill plot

Grid of violin+boxplots — rows = Spearman rho, RMSE (log-scale); columns =
Biomass / Catch / Mean individual weight. All three indicators compare
modelled vs observed values directly. RMSE is computed on log-transformed
values throughout, expressing error as an order-of-magnitude discrepancy
rather than being dominated by whichever species/years have the largest
absolute biomass, catch, or mean weight. **Higher rho / lower RMSE = better
model–observation agreement for that scenario.**

```{r skill-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
p_sk <- ggplot(skill, aes(x = scen, y = value, fill = scen)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, trim = FALSE, width = 0.9) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.size = 0.3, fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  facet_grid(stat_type ~ indicator, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Factual (seal increase)"         = "red",
                               "Counterfactual (seals constant)" = "blue")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

# Save skill plot: a quick local debug copy, and the "real" copy in save_dir
ggsave("indicator_model_skill.png", p_sk, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "indicator_model_skill.jpeg"), p_sk, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 200)

p_sk
```
